hotspots.description: Logs, ropes, the net, the mud, the wall, then the targets. Every Ashigaru runs it at dawn; the record is chalked on the post by the door.

spotConfig.label: Check the route marker
spotConfig.text: A post carved with the Ashigaru sprout and an arrow: HUB, three hours. Someone has re-cut the arrow fresh this week. The road is open.

spotConfig.label: Check the route marker
spotConfig.text: The east marker leans, but its runner knots are still tied: one for each runner who passed today. Seven knots.

spotConfig.label: Check the route marker
spotConfig.text: The west marker has a crack running up it from the ground, red dust in the crack. It still stands, and its arrow still points true.

spotConfig.label: Light the starter lantern
spotConfig.text: The wick catches at the second try. A small warm light by the bridge: the first thing a traveller sees of the village.

spotConfig.label: Light the starter lantern
spotConfig.text: You light the lantern by the inner gate. The guard nods without looking round, as if he had been waiting for it.

spotConfig.label: Light the starter lantern
spotConfig.text: The last lantern lights the road up to the square. Now the way in is lit all the way, gate to well.

spotConfig.label: Look at the sprout
spotConfig.text: A single sprout, growing out of the stream at the bottom of the moat. Two leaves, like the mark on every Ashigaru banner. Nobody planted it.
From the top of the logs you can see over the stakes: the moat, the bridge, the long road to the Hub, and three watchtowers on the far hills you never noticed before.

spotConfig.label: Start the moat walk
spotConfig.startText: The whole way round the moat, to the far side of the bridge. Take your time.
spotConfig.failText: You climbed out of the moat. Start again at the marker by the bridge.
spotConfig.text: You come out of the moat on the far side of the bridge, muddy to the knees. The whole ring, every step. The runners do this every morning.

riddle.title: The Sprout's Riddle
riddle.solvedText: Carried in, counted, grown into a home: growth through endurance. The sprout carved on the well looks a little greener.

parts.text: I begin as a seed, and a seed must be carried in from outside. Stand where the road passes between the two towers.
Before a seed is planted it is counted, and its name is written down. Go to the house that keeps their names.
Last: find what was a forest once and is waiting to become a home.

riddleAnswer.text: Through the gate between the two towers: the seed is in.
The Seed Archive, where every seed has a name.
The strategy hall keeps plans, not seeds.
The log pile. Every log here was a seed once.

riddles.q: A farmer has three haystacks in one field and five in the next. He carries them all into one field. How many haystacks does he have?
riddles.why: Put together, they make one big haystack.

riddles.q: The more of them you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?
riddles.why: Every step you take leaves a footprint behind you.

riddles.q: When the squad lines up three abreast, two are left over. Four abreast: three left over. Five abreast: four left over. What is the smallest the squad can be?
riddles.why: One more Rebel and every line would be full: 60 fills rows of three, four and five. So the squad is 59.

riddles.q: I have a foot but never walk, a peak but never point, and I grow no taller in a thousand years. What am I?
riddles.why: The foot of the mountain, the peak of the mountain: it stands where it stood.

riddles.q: Sawing a log into 4 pieces takes 12 minutes. At the same pace, how long does it take to saw a log into 8 pieces?
riddles.why: Four pieces need three cuts: four minutes a cut. Eight pieces need seven cuts: 28 minutes.

riddles.q: Aki, Ben and Chiyo each grow one crop: rice, millet or beans. Aki does not grow rice. Chiyo does not grow beans. Ben grows millet. Who grows the rice?
riddles.why: Ben has the millet, so Aki (no rice) has the beans, and the rice is left to Chiyo, who was never the bean farmer.

riddles.q: Four fields lie in a row, west to east. Millet is at the west end. The beans are not next to the millet. The barley is east of the beans. The rice is next to the beans. What grows at the east end?
riddles.why: The beans can only be third (not beside the millet, with barley still east of them). Barley is fourth and rice second.

riddles.q: Two guards stand at the gate: one always tells the truth, one always lies. The first says: "At least one of us is a liar." Which one tells the truth?
riddles.why: A liar could never say that true thing about himself, so the first speaks the truth, and the second is the liar.

riddles.q: A farmer ant is four times as old as her son. In twenty years she will be only twice as old. How old is the son now?
riddles.why: Four times his age plus twenty is twice his age plus forty: his age is ten (she is forty).

riddles.q: Rice and millet weigh 30 together, millet and beans 35, rice and beans 25. How heavy is the millet?
riddles.why: All three pairs add up to twice everything: 90, so everything is 45. Take away rice and beans (25): the millet is 20.

riddles.q: Exactly one of three farmers stole the seed. Aki says: "Ben did it." Ben says: "I did not." Chiyo says: "I did not." Only one of them tells the truth. Who stole the seed?
riddles.why: If Chiyo did it, only Ben speaks the truth. Any other thief would make two of them truthful.

riddles.q: Lilies on the paddy pond double every day. On the thirtieth day they cover the whole pond. On which day did they cover half of it?
riddles.why: They double each day, so the day before the pond was full it was half full.

riddles.q: One farmer ploughs a field in 3 days, another in 6 days. Ploughing the same field together, how many days do they need?
riddles.why: Each day the first does a third and the second a sixth: half a field a day together, so two days.

riddles.q: Three huts stand in a row, west to east, with red, blue and green roofs. The green hut is in the middle. The rice farmer lives east of the blue hut. The millet farmer lives under the red roof. The bean farmer lives west of the millet farmer. What colour is the rice farmer's roof?
riddles.why: Someone lives east of blue, so blue is the west hut and red the east one, the millet farmer's. The beans are west of the millet, and the rice is east of blue but not under red: the green middle hut.

riddles.q: A sack of rice and a sack of beans cost 110 coins together. The rice costs 100 coins more than the beans. What do the beans cost?
riddles.why: Beans 5 and rice 105: together 110, and the rice is 100 more. (Ten would make the rice 110 and the pair 120.)

riddles.q: Ants and cranes walk in a field: 12 heads and 40 legs between them. An ant has six legs, a crane two. How many ants are there?
riddles.why: Twelve cranes would have 24 legs; each ant in place of a crane adds four more. 16 more legs: four ants (and eight cranes).

riddles.q: Sawing a log into 4 pieces takes 12 minutes. A farmer saws a second log into 2 pieces and a third into 6 pieces. How long do the two logs take, at the same pace?
riddles.why: Four pieces take three cuts: four minutes a cut. One cut and five cuts make six cuts: 24 minutes.
